thread:
danielle: Heads-up — Acme reported a possible vuln during a snapshot restore. They restored a backup from last year and noticed old audit entries reappearing tied to different key IDs. They're asking if data could be exposed and want an ETA for a fix. Marking P0 from customer side. :rotating_light:

chris: Copy — can you paste the snapshot id + any logs they gave? Also did they do a cross-account restore or same account?

 danielle: snapshot id: snap-2026-04-11-8571 (redacted). Same account restore. Customer pasted this log line:

```
2026-04-11T14:02:12Z restore started snapshot=snap-2026-04-11-8571 tenant=acme action=apply wrap_key_id=ek-9xx legacy_wrap_meta=true
2026-04-11T14:02:13Z audit log reimported id=log-2022-11-03 source=old_index
```

maria: :eyes: that legacy_wrap_meta flag is suspicious. Sounds like the restore flow re-associated wrapped keys from the snapshot without rewrapping them under the current tenant KEK. Could allow older ciphertext to be accepted by the runtime if KEK chain changed. Creating an internal P0 incident. @kevin can we toggle restore endpoint for that tenant and prevent new restores while we triage?

kevin: I can add a tenant-level deny for /v1/snapshots/restore in the edge policy. Will push a kill-switch to staging in ~8m, prod in ~25-30m if tests pass.

maria: Good. We also need a short mitigation for the customer: rotate the tenant KEK immediately and rotate dataset DEKs where possible. If they can pause automated restores that reduces window. Example rewrap flow we can ask them to run (we'll provide support):

```bash
# rotate tenant KEK (managed)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/kms/tenants/acme/rotate

# rewrap dataset key (example)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"dataset_id":"ds-123","action":"rewrap"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/kms/keys/rewrap
```

danielle: Sending those steps now. Customer asked for an official timeline for patching and whether this maps to a CVE.

legal: Please capture exact evidence (snapshots, logs, who requested restore) and timeline. We need to evaluate breach/disclosure obligations. cc: security-compliance.

oncall-eng: Pushed logs from the restore run — we see entries where wrap_key_id is null for a short window and then restored objects reference legacy key IDs. Looks like edge accepts legacy wrap metadata on import.

sre-bot: Incident created INC-2026-742 (severity P0). Oncall paged.

chris: I'm drafting the customer update: pause restores, rotate KEK, run rewrap. Also asked them to export any suspicious audit lines and confirm whether any external access occurred.

maria: Root cause (prelim): restore path applies snapshot metadata blobs directly without forcing a re-encryption step when legacy_wrap_meta=true. Fix plan: require rewrap-on-restore (force DEK re-encryption under current KEK) and validate wrap metadata during import. Backport targets: 1.4.x and 1.5.x (customers still on older stacks). Timeline: hotfix PR ready in ~45m, deploy to prod in ~2h after canary; advisory + CVE filing within 24h if confirmed.

kevin: Toggle deployed to prod (tenant block) at 14:30 UTC. Observability shows restores are now blocked for acme. Rolling patch pipeline started for staging.

danielle: Customer updated with mitigation + tentative timeline. They asked for written SLA impact note for their legal team.

maria: We'll prepare a short incident summary for SLAs and compliance; security will draft the advisory. Keep collecting evidence and any signs of exfil.

chris: I'll follow up with the customer after the hotfix deploy and share the advisory draft.

danielle: Thanks everyone — will update thread with any customer replies.
